title: Lotus Principal Resolution Denial Fixture
description: One hostile case a consumer must prove it refuses. A consumer that passes only the positive case has not implemented RFC-0109. Each fixture states the request shape, the posture it is evaluated under, and the exact refusal required.

environmentPosture.description: Every denial fixture is evaluated under `verified`. Under `header-trust` the perimeter is the control, and these cases do not apply.

verifierOutcome.description: What the consumer's own verifier must return for this credential: 'accept' or 'reject'. This is an instruction to the test harness, not a property of the payload. The fixture carries no signed bytes and no keys, so it cannot compel cryptographic verification -- a consumer that maps this value to a result rather than configuring its verifier proves nothing. See the limitation named in README.md.

assertedHeaders.description: Headers the caller supplied. Under `verified` these carry no authority; they are recorded so a fixture can prove they were ignored rather than honoured.

actingForSubjectRef.description: Present only for delegated calls: the user the application is acting for.

failsAtStep.description: Which resolution step refuses. A denial at a later step than expected means an earlier control did not run.

revealsReasonDetail.description: A denial states its class and nothing further.

maxProtectedOperationCalls.description: How many calls the refusal path may make to the protected operation the request was trying to perform. Zero for every denial: a refusal must precede every effect it disclaims. Resolution lookups are deliberately excluded -- key discovery, tenant membership and the grant store are how the refusal is reached, and grant_store_unavailable can only be discovered by attempting that call. A boolean cannot distinguish no calls from nobody counting, so the consumer asserts a number against a recording client.
